title: Bkerki rally supporting the Maronite Patriarch’s neutrality call
location: Outside the Maronite Patriarchate in Bkerki
participants_original: The961’s headline says “Thousands”; the article body says “a large number” and gives no numeric count or method.
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporaneous page headline describes thousands at this rally, while its body uses only “a large number”; this is an attributed qualitative outlet claim and has no disclosed counting method. The body describes the gathering as peaceful.

start_date.summary: The article dateline is Feb. 27, 2021; it labels the demonstration as Saturday and separately notes a Feb. 28 page update. The update is not treated as event duration.

location.summary: The text places the gathering outside the Maronite Patriarchate at Bkerki.

demands.summary: The outlet says the crowd supported Patriarch Bechara al-Rahi’s call for neutrality and an international conference, alongside appeals to Lebanese officials to work across sectarian barriers. Whether this support rally itself constituted a demand to the State remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: The headline says “Thousands,” while the body says “a large number” without a numeric estimate or method; no range is inferred.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened article’s headline reports thousands, sufficient as an attributed outlet claim to clear 50; no exact count or counting method is available.

protester_violence.summary: The article describes the demonstration as peaceful; no separate event-wide incident account is given.

open_questions: Does support for the patriarch’s national policy call establish a demand directed at the Lebanese State, given the spokesperson’s statement that the event was not political?
Can the rally’s crowd size be independently verified beyond the outlet headline?
What was the physical end time/date? Unknown.
notes: This is a Feb. 27 physical gathering. It is not merged with the Jan. 25–28 Tripoli anti-lockdown episode or the possible Jan. 31 Tripoli resumption; no continuity relationship is evidenced.

title: Feb. 15 military-court sit-in for release of Tripoli detainees
location: Outside the Military Court in Beirut
participants_original: LBCI reports “a number of protesters,” with no numerical count.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established: “a number of” provides no numeric count or lower bound of 50. Retain as a physical gathering lead with pending threshold.

start_date.summary: The LBCI dateline is Feb. 15, 2021 and the article says the sit-in was held on Monday.

location.summary: LBCI places the gathering outside the Military Court in Beirut.

demands.summary: The stated demand was release of people arrested after the Tripoli riots.

participants_original.summary: The article says “a number of protesters,” without a numerical estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence in this source supports at least 50 participants.

open_questions: What was its physical end time/date?
How does this dated Feb. 15 sit-in relate to the separately reported Feb. 5–13 court gatherings?
notes: A distinct Feb. 15 physical Beirut sit-in is established; it is not a Tripoli lockdown action and is not merged with other court gatherings without unit-level evidence.
